_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Tech Mahindra (consolidated, Rs crore). Revenue is built in USD by vertical (usdBuild), converted at the stated INR/USD path; revenueGrowth below is that build expressed in rupees (checked in tools/authoring/TECHM.ctx.js). Margins are set on the company's EBIT definition; the engine's EBITDA margin = EBIT margin + depreciation as a % of revenue (the engine's own depreciation). History is attributable profit and reported basic EPS (tools/authoring/TECHM.patch.js: TML Benefit Trust treasury shares excluded, ~88.6 cr shares). Valued on P/E, as the street does.

usdBuild._why: FY27: Q1 USD 1,660 mn (+6.1% YoY reported, +6.6% CC, organic +6.2%); Q2 loses 1-1.3% from the European auto programme delivered early in Q1, offset by a large telecom deal that had not started ramping and the end of a cloud pass-through drag; we assume ~+1% QoQ in Q2 and ~1.5% in Q3-Q4, i.e. FY27 USD 6,772 mn (+6.1%), in line with brokers (USD 6,745-6,792 mn). By vertical: communications +3.5% (Q1 +1.3% YoY; deal ramp vs 'volatility in a large US telecoms client'), manufacturing +12% (Q1 +17.2%, aerospace, auto pull-forward), BFSI +9% (Q1 +8.1% plus the Avant acquisition), TME +2% (volatile client spend), retail/logistics +8%, healthcare +7%. FY28-29: +5% a year, below the street's 5-7.5% for FY28: once the large-deal ramps are in the base, Tech Mahindra faces the same AI deflation as peers (HCLTech: legacy revenue erosion of 2-3% a year; peers guide 1-4% CC for FY27). Constant-currency growth assumed equal to reported after FY27 (no cross-currency view).
usdBuild._fxWhy: INR/USD averaged 89.0 in FY26, 94.6 in Q1FY27 and closed 95.81-95.83 on 30-Sep-2026. Forecasts published by then: BMI 97 by Mar-2027 and 99 by Mar-2028; Axis Bank 97 by Dec-2026 and 100 by Jun-2027. We use 95.5 / 97.0 / 98.5 (about 1.5% depreciation a year), the cautious end of those forecasts.

_revWhy: INR revenue = USD build x INR/USD path: Rs64,671 cr (FY27E), Rs68,977 cr (FY28E), Rs73,559 cr (FY29E). FY27's 13.8% rupee growth is 6.1% in dollars plus 7.3% from the weaker rupee (89.0 to 95.5).
_marginWhy: EBIT (company definition) 6.1% (FY24), 9.7% (FY25), 12.6% (FY26), 14.4% in Q1FY27 after 11 straight quarters of expansion; management targets 15% for FY27 and says Q4FY27 'has to be upwards of 15%'. Q2 carries phased wage hikes and the auto reversal, so FY27E 14.8% (Q1 14.4, ~14.3 Q2, ~15.0 Q3, ~15.4 Q4), within the street's 14.6-15.1%. FY28E 15.3% and FY29E 15.6%: a weaker rupee (+1.5% a year) and fixed-price productivity help, but the onsite-heavy large deals, AI investment and productivity pass-backs in renewals cap the gain; management has not set a target beyond FY27. Street FY28E 14.8-15.9%. The engine needs EBITDA margin: EBIT margin + depreciation (engine) of Rs1,962 / 2,015 / 2,071 cr = 3.03% / 2.92% / 2.82% of revenue.
_capexWhy: Cash capex Rs1,015 cr (FY23), Rs791 cr (FY24), Rs594 cr (FY25), Rs696 cr (FY26): ~1.1-1.3% of revenue for an asset-light services firm (offices, computers, software). Rs850-950 cr (~1.3% of revenue) allows for the new experience centres in Pune and Hyderabad mentioned on the Q1FY27 call. Leased offices (right-of-use assets) are outside capex.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs1,882 cr = 6.2% of average gross block (Rs30,426 cr, incl. intangibles and right-of-use assets); Q1FY27 Rs479 cr (Rs1,916 cr annualised). The engine grows gross block only with capex (lease additions are not modelled), so 6.1% gives Rs1,962 cr in FY27E, close to the run-rate.
_treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net treasury (cash Rs5,105 cr + investments Rs3,426 cr - borrowings incl. leases Rs2,186 cr = Rs6,345 cr at Mar-26). FY26 treasury income (interest Rs98 cr + gains on FVTPL investments Rs154 cr + dividends Rs0.3 cr = Rs252 cr; AR FY26 note 29) was 3.1% of average gross cash and investments (~Rs8,000 cr, much of it held abroad at low rates) and 4.2% of average net treasury (Rs6,022 cr). 4.0% on net treasury = Rs254 cr in FY27E.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income = miscellaneous and rental income less FX losses. Misc + rental: Rs252 cr in FY26 (misc Rs234 cr incl. fair-value changes of acquisition obligations, rental Rs18 cr), Rs311 cr in FY25; we use Rs190 / 200 / 210 cr. FX (hedge and translation) losses: -USD 52 mn in FY26 (Rs480 cr), -USD 23 mn (~Rs218 cr) in Q1FY27 as the rupee fell from 85.3 to 94.6. The hedge book shrank from USD 1.96 bn (Mar-25) to USD 0.72 bn (Jun-26) with tenor cut to one year, so most hedges written before the fall have matured; Q2FY27 still carries a ~1.4% rupee fall. FX: -Rs400 cr (FY27E: Q1 actual -218, ~-80 in Q2, ~-50 a quarter in H2), -Rs100 cr (FY28E), -Rs50 cr (FY29E). Total other income FY27E ~Rs44 cr vs Rs32 cr in FY26 and -Rs292 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 (ex the Rs272 cr Labour Code charge); the gap to the TTM is the FX line (TTM -Rs720 cr). Ex-FX, FY27E (Rs444 cr) equals Q1FY27 annualised (Rs111 cr x 4) and is below FY26 (Rs510 cr).
_interestLabel: Finance costs (mainly interest on lease liabilities)
_interestWhy: Rs326 cr (FY23), Rs392 cr (FY24), Rs322 cr (FY25), Rs337 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs111 cr as lease liabilities rose to Rs2,117 cr (Mar-26) from Rs1,554 cr. Borrowings excluding leases are only ~Rs70 cr.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (no minority line in the engine). FY26 effective tax 27% (24.3% in Q4); management: FY27 'in a similar range'. Q1FY27: tax Rs556 cr + minorities Rs21 cr on PBT Rs2,042 cr = 28.2%. Minorities are partners in Comviva and other subsidiaries.
_payoutWhy: Policy: at least 85% of free cash flow over five years as dividends and/or buybacks. FY26: Rs51 a share (interim 15 + final 36) = 94% of basic EPS and 91% of FCF; FY25 Rs45 = 94%. FCF has run at 100-115% of PAT, so 85% of EPS is the policy floor, not a forecast of cuts.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, but a mid-tier IT exporter with a volatile earnings history (FY24 EPS halved) and heavy telecom exposure: beta 1.0, Ke 12.5%.
dcf._tgWhy: Rupee revenue growth of 5% after FY38 = ~2-3% dollar growth (AI deflation eats part of volume) plus ~2% rupee depreciation; the low end of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Rupee revenue growth fades from 6.6% (FY29E) to 5% over twelve years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin ~18.4% in FY29E (EBIT 15.6%) eases to 18%: pricing pressure from AI pass-backs offsets further productivity; Tech Mahindra has never sustained an EBIT margin above ~15%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Large-deal ramps and above-peer growth persist (USD ~7% a year in FY28-29), AI work grows faster than legacy work shrinks, and the margin keeps rising to ~16.5% by FY29 on pyramid and rupee tailwinds; the sector partly re-rates.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI deflation reaches Tech Mahindra's run contracts and communications clients (USD growth ~2% a year after FY27), the 15% margin is missed as pricing gives back productivity, and the stock trades like the de-rated Tier-1 peers.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Tech Mahindra: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E or Jun-28E EPS (16.9-20x; Jul-Sep 2026). 16x = the stock's 23.3x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on reported EPS (house trough rule: FY24 left out; 26.0x with it, 21.2x if FY25 is also left out, 23.8x on EPS before the FY25-26 one-offs) cut by the 31.3% median de-rating of the nine-stock IT peer set versus each stock's five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (TCS -53%, Infosys -49%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, LTTS -31%, Mphasis -27%, HCLTech -21%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%) = 16.0x. No further growth or returns adjustment (a justified P/E at our 12.5% cost of equity, 6.5% growth and 85% payout is 15.1x, so returns do not argue for more). Bull 18x (the stock's FY28E multiple today; Elara and Nomura). Bear 13x (the incumbents-only de-rating of -44.5% applied to 23.3x = 12.9x; Infosys and Wipro trade at 12-13x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 9x Sep-28E EBITDA = the stock's 12.7x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (FY24 left out; EV on the 88.6 cr shares outside the TML Benefit Trust) less the same 31.3% sector de-rating = 8.7x. Bull 10x (today's forward multiple), bear 7x (incumbents-only de-rating).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5%, plus net cash.
